newsitem.title: USA: NYS Senate urges letting voters decide on casinos.
newsitem.headline: NYS Senate urges letting voters decide on casinos.

text.p: The New York Senate Majority Leader on Monday, admitting he probably did not have enough votes to get a casino bill approved, urged lawmakers to send the measure to the voters to let them decide.

"People are on their own, this is not political, not partisan, if people feel that the people ought to have a right to vote in a referendum, they'll vote up, and if they don't, they won't. That'll be the issue," Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, told reporters at a news conference in Albany.

The measure, which would permit one casino in Buffalo, Niagara Falls and either Warren or Saratoga County, faces strong opposition and is expected to be voted on by the Republican-controlled Senate on Tuesday.
The Catskills, whose resorts have declined, would be able to build an unlimited number of casinos if the bill were approved.
While a previous legislature approved the bill, it must win another vote before it can be sent to the voters in a referendum.
